source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-115: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 115 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume a multi-node GPU collective intends to use RoCE, but verify the actual transport and any host-staged or alternate fallback path. Begin with authorized read-only collection: document GPU/NIC PCIe and NVLink affinity, topology, firmware and driver versions, link speed, MTU, VLAN/priority mapping, PFC/ECN, route symmetry, queue pairs, memory registration, message sizes, concurrency, placement, and clock synchronization. A falsifiable hypothesis is that congestion or a priority/route/MTU mismatch creates queueing and raises p99.9 while p50 and the controlled workload remain stable; host scheduling and workload drift are competing explanations. Correlate synchronized application and verbs/completion timestamps with NIC retries, errors, drops and ECN, switch queue depth and PFC pause counters where available. Report p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency in ms, throughput, completion errors, retries, timeouts, sample counts and uncertainty using interleaved matched baseline and treatment runs. Do not infer causality from one mean. Preserve and redact logs. Any change needs owner authorization, a snapshot, one-variable canary, correctness checks, and a defined rollback; revert if correctness fails, timeouts/errors rise, or the agreed tail-latency guardrail worsens. If switch counters or transport visibility are unavailable, label the diagnosis evidence_required rather than guessing vendor-specific behavior.
risks: RoCE behavior depends on NIC, switch, driver, firmware, priority mapping, and whether GPU-direct is actually active.
Tail metrics can be confounded by workload placement, CPU scheduling, clock skew, and fallback transport.
evidence_required: Synchronized application/verbs timestamps, NIC and switch counters, topology and transport-selection evidence, and interleaved baseline/treatment samples.
Owner authorization, configuration snapshots, correctness results, and rollback-trigger observations before any mutation.

source_user: Advanced cluster case GDR-2: Design a validation plan for GPUDirect RDMA between GPUs and NICs. Variant 2 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: verify topology and peer access, registration and pinning, IOMMU/container permissions, NIC-GPU affinity, direct versus staged copies, and compare bandwidth and CPU utilization. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume the platform and container are authorized and that GPUDirect RDMA is intended, but do not infer direct GPU access from configuration labels. Establish a read-only baseline and record GPU/NIC PCIe topology and affinity, peer-access capability, driver/firmware/runtime versions, IOMMU and container permissions, memory registration and pinning behavior, link and message sizes, concurrency, placement, and clocking. A falsifiable hypothesis is that the direct GPU-to-NIC path is active and improves effective bandwidth while reducing host CPU utilization versus an otherwise matched host-staged path; a missing permission, unsupported topology, registration fault, or fallback path should invalidate it. Use synchronized transfer/completion timestamps and report bandwidth in GB/s, latency in ms, CPU utilization, errors/timeouts, sample counts, and percentile uncertainty across interleaved direct, staged, and appropriate controls. Verify data correctness and detect fallback rather than relying on nominal settings. Preserve redacted evidence. Any change requires owner authorization, a snapshot, a reversible canary, correctness gates, and rollback if errors/timeouts occur, correctness differs, or the agreed performance guardrail regresses; unavailable topology or vendor-specific evidence remains evidence_required.
risks: GPUDirect RDMA may silently fall back to host staging or be blocked by topology, IOMMU, registration, or container permissions.
Bandwidth and CPU results depend on message size, concurrency, affinity, NUMA placement, clocks, and competing workload.
evidence_required: Topology/peer-access and permission checks, registration logs, transport-path evidence, synchronized timings, bandwidth/CPU measurements, and correctness results.
Matched direct/staged baselines with sample counts, percentiles, workload parameters, and authorized rollback criteria.
